newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds flat in sympathy with U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds flat in sympathy with U.S. holiday.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat early Monday in virtually zero trade on account of the Columbus Day holiday in the U.S.
"There is no activity today," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 119.10, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 was steady at 83-1/4.
While trade was at a near standstill, analysts said the market was likely to firm later in the week.
"We recommend to take advantage of the last downside movement of the market, going long as a medium term strategy," said analysts at Banco Rio de la Plata in an investor note.
"Considering that fundamentals have not worsened, we do not find reasons to change our positive medium term forecast."
All the same, traders and analysts said the release of the U.S. consumer price index on Wednesday was reason for investors to remain on the sidelines until the figure is known.
